member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ContextMenuSettings
member.summary: Represents the settings for a context menu (shortcut menu) in a diagram component.

remarks.para: The class enables customization of context menus in diagram components. Configure menu visibility, define custom items, and handle menu events through this component.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent @ref="diagram" Height="600px" Width="90%" @bind-Nodes="nodes" >
            <ContextMenuSettings @bind-Show="@show" @bind-ShowCustomMenuOnly="@customMenuOnly" @bind-Items="@Items" ContextMenuOpening="@BeforeOpen" ContextMenuItemClicked="@ItemClicked">
            </ContextMenuSettings>
            </SfDiagramComponent>
             @code {
            SfDiagramComponent diagram;
            DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
            ContextMenuSettings ContextMenuSettings;
            List<ContextMenuItem> Items;
            bool customMenuOnly = false;
            bool show = true;
            protected override void OnInitialized()
            {
            
                Items = new List<ContextMenuItem>()
                {
                         new ContextMenuItem()
                        {
                            Text = "Save As...",
                            Id = "save",
                            IconCss = "e-save",
                        },
                        new ContextMenuItem()
                        {
                            Text = "Group",
                            Id = "load",
                            IconCss = "e-group"
                        }
                };
               Node node = new Node()
               {
                 // Position of the node
                 OffsetX = 250,
                 OffsetY = 250,
                 // Size of the node
                 Width = 100,
                 Height = 100,
                   };
                   nodes.Add(node);
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ContextMenuSettings.Show
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the context menu (shortcut menu) is displayed in the diagram component.
member.value: true if the context menu can be enabled; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: By default, the property is set to false which disables the context menu; set this property to true to enable the context menu functionality.
When enabled, the context menu will appear when users perform a right-click action on diagram elements, providing quick access to contextual commands and operations.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ContextMenuSettings.Items
member.summary: Gets or sets the collection of ContextMenuItem objects that define the items displayed in the context menu.
member.value: A collection of objects or null.

remarks.para: Defines the menu items displayed when the context menu is triggered. Each item represents a menu option with text, icon, and actions.

example.para: The following example demonstrates how to configure context menu items
example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent>
            <ContextMenuSettings  @bind-Items="@Items" >
            </ContextMenuSettings>
             </SfDiagramComponent>
             @code {
            protected override void OnInitialized()
            {
            
                Items = new List<ContextMenuItem>()
                {
                         new ContextMenuItem()
                        {
                            Text = "Save As...",
                            Id = "save",
                            IconCss = "e-save",
                        },
                };
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ContextMenuSettings.ShowCustomMenuOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether only the custom menu items are displayed in the context menu.

remarks.para: By default, ShowCustomMenuOnly is set to false. Set this property to true to display only custom menu items.

member.value: A boolean value where true displays only custom menu items, and false displays both default and custom menu items.

example.code:
<ContextMenuSettings @bind-Show="@show" @bind-ShowCustomMenuOnly="@customMenuOnly" >
             </ContextMenuSettings>
             @code {
             bool customMenuOnly = false;
             bool show = true;
             protected override void OnInitialized()

             }

member.summary: Represents the properties common to both horizontal and vertical rulers for measuring the diagram area.

remarks.para: This base class provides properties shared between and for defining their appearance and behavior in the diagram component.
The ruler provides visual measurement guides that help users align and position elements within the diagram canvas.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramRuler.IsVisible
member.summary: Gets or sets the value indicating whether the horizontal and vertical rulers are visible in the diagram.

remarks.para: Controls the visibility of the ruler component. When true, the ruler is displayed; when false, it is hidden.
Horizontal and vertical rulers can be shown or hidden separately as needed.

member.value: The default value of IsVisible is true.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure ruler visibility
<SfDiagramComponent Height = "600px"> <RulerSettings> <HorizontalRuler IsVisible = "true"/> <VerticalRuler IsVisible = "true"/> </RulerSettings> </SfDiagramComponent>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramRuler.Interval
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of intervals to be present on each segment of the ruler.
member.value: The default intervals in a segment of the ruler is 5.

remarks.para: Controls how many small marks appear on each ruler section. Higher numbers show more marks, lower numbers show fewer marks.
This setting works for both horizontal and vertical rulers to keep measurements consistent.

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure ruler intervals
<SfDiagramComponent Height = "600px"> <RulerSettings> <HorizontalRuler Interval = "7"> </HorizontalRuler> </RulerSettings> </SfDiagramComponent>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramRuler.SegmentWidth

member.value: The default segment width of the ruler is 100.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramRuler.TickAlignment
member.summary: Gets or sets the alignment of tick marks in the ruler.
member.value: The default value is .

remarks.para: Controls the positioning of tick marks relative to the ruler's baseline. The alignment determines whether ticks appear on the left/top side, right/bottom side, or both sides of the ruler line.
For more info regarding TickAlignment, refer to

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure ruler tick alignment
<SfDiagramComponent Height = "600px"> <RulerSettings> <HorizontalRuler TickAlignment = "TickAlignment.RightAndBottom"> </HorizontalRuler> </RulerSettings> </SfDiagramComponent>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramRuler.MarkerColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the color of the marker line that tracks the cursor position on the ruler.
member.value: The default value of MarkerColor is "red".

remarks.para: This property controls the visual appearance of the dynamic marker line that follows the cursor position within the diagram area.
The marker line serves as a visual guide to help users precisely align elements and understand their current position relative to the ruler's measurement scale.

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure ruler marker color
<SfDiagramComponent Height = "600px"> <RulerSettings> <HorizontalRuler Interval = "7" MarkerColor = "blue"> </HorizontalRuler> </RulerSettings> </SfDiagramComponent>

The padding to start the auto-scrolling at the edge can be controlled by setting the property.

The following example demonstrates how to enable auto-scrolling in the diagram.
<SfDiagramComponent Width="1000px" Height="1000px"> <ScrollSettings EnableAutoScroll="true"> </ScrollSettings> </SfDiagramComponent>

remarks.para: The automatic scrolling region is calculated as a distance from the edge of the viewport equal to the value of the padding. For example, if the right padding is set to 5 pixels, the auto-scroll start region will be 5 pixels from the inner edge of the right viewport edge.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramGridLines
member.summary: Represents the visual guidance lines displayed while dragging or arranging objects in the .

remarks.para: Provides configuration options for customizing grid line appearance and behavior during object manipulation.
Grid lines serve as visual guides for precise alignment and positioning of diagram elements.
Horizontal and vertical grid lines can be styled independently, with visibility controlled by constraints.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramGridLines.LineColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the color of the horizontal or vertical grid lines in the .
member.value: A representing the color value for the grid lines. The default value is "LIGHTGRAY".

remarks.para: Accepts standard CSS color formats including named colors, hexadecimal, RGB, and RGBA values.
Affects the visual appearance of grid lines used as alignment guides during diagram manipulation.

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set the color of the horizontal and vertical grid lines to blue.
<SfDiagramComponent> <SnapSettings Constraints="SnapConstraints.ShowLines"> <HorizontalGridLines LineColor="blue" > </HorizontalGridLines> <VerticalGridLines LineColor="blue"> </VerticalGridLines> </SnapSettings> </SfDiagramComponent> @code { }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramGridLines.LineDashArray
member.summary: Gets or sets the pattern of dashes and gaps used to render the horizontal or vertical grid lines in the .
member.value: A representing the dash pattern as a space-separated list of numbers defining dash and gap lengths. The default value is .

remarks.para: Specify dash patterns using space-separated numeric values (e.g., "5 3" for 5-unit dashes with 3-unit gaps). When or , renders solid lines.

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure dashed grid lines with different patterns.
<SfDiagramComponent> <SnapSettings Constraints="SnapConstraints.ShowLines"> <HorizontalGridLines LineDashArray="2" > </HorizontalGridLines> <VerticalGridLines LineDashArray="2"> </VerticalGridLines> </SnapSettings> </SfDiagramComponent> @code { }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramGridLines.LineIntervals
member.summary: Gets or sets the line intervals that define the thickness and spacing between horizontal or vertical grid lines in the .
member.value: A array representing the alternating pattern of line thickness and spacing values for grid lines. The default value is { 1.25, 18.75, 0.25, 19.75, 0.25, 19.75, 0.25, 19.75, 0.25, 19.75 }.

remarks.para: The array defines alternating line thickness and spacing values that repeat cyclically to create the grid pattern. Values are measured in diagram units.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramGridLines.DotIntervals
member.summary: Gets or sets the pattern of gaps defined by a set of dots for the Gridlines.
member.value: A [] representing the dot interval pattern for grid lines. The default value is { 1, 19, 0.5, 19.5, 0.5, 19.5, 0.5, 19.5, 0.5, 19.5 }.

remarks.para: Defines a repeating pattern where values alternate between dot thickness and spacing to create the visual grid structure. The pattern repeats cyclically and is measured in diagram units.
Setting this property to will use the default dot pattern.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramGridLines.SnapIntervals
member.summary: Gets or sets a set of intervals for snapping objects in the . By default, objects are snapped towards the nearest grid line.
member.value: A array representing the snap intervals for grid lines. The default value is { 20 }.

remarks.para: Defines the spacing between grid lines for object snapping. Each value represents a distance interval in diagram units.
Setting this property to will use default snapping behavior. Values should be positive numbers.

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set custom snap intervals for both horizontal and vertical grid lines.
<SfDiagramComponent> <SnapSettings Constraints="SnapConstraints.ShowLines"> <HorizontalGridLines SnapIntervals="30" > </HorizontalGridLines> <VerticalGridLines SnapIntervals="30" > </VerticalGridLines> </SnapSettings> </SfDiagramComponent> @code { }

member.summary: Represents the snap settings that customize and control the grid lines and snap behavior of the .

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.GridPanel
member.summary: Represents a panel that arranges its child elements in a grid. The `GridPanel` is a layout panel provided by the SfDiagramComponent for organizing its child elements in a grid-based structure. It allows you to define rows and columns and place the child elements in the desired position within the grid.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height = "1000px" Width="1000px" BasicElements="@basicElements" >
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code {
            DiagramObjectCollection<CommonElement> basicElements = new DiagramObjectCollection<CommonElement>();
            protected override void OnInitialized()
            {
               GridPanel gridPanel = new GridPanel()
               {
                   ID = "grid1",
                   Height = 100,
                   Width = 100,
                   OffsetX = 300,
                   OffsetY = 200,
                   Style = new ShapeStyle() { Fill = "Red" }
               };
               basicElements.Add(gridPanel);
            }
            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.GridPanel.AddObject(Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramElement,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Adds a child object to the grid at the specified position with optional row and column spans.
member.param: The child object to add to the grid.
The row index at which to place the child object.
The column index at which to place the child object.
The number of rows that the child object should span. Defaults to 0, which indicates no row span.
The number of columns that the child object should span. Defaults to 0, which indicates no column span.
member.remarks: This method allows you to add a child object to the grid at a specific position defined by the row and column indices. The optional row and column spans determine how many rows and columns the child object should occupy within the grid.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height = "2000px" Width="850px" BasicElements="@basicElements" >
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code {
                DiagramObjectCollection<CommonElement> basicElements = new DiagramObjectCollection<CommonElement>();
                    protected override void OnInitialized()
                    {
                        GridPanel grid = new GridPanel();
                        grid.OffsetX = 300;
                        grid.OffsetY = 200;
                        List<RowDefinition> rowDefns = new List<RowDefinition>();
                        RowDefinition rowDefn1 = new RowDefinition();
                        rowDefn1.Height = 50;
                        rowDefns.Add(rowDefn1);
                        RowDefinition rowDefn2 = new RowDefinition();
                        rowDefn2.Height = 50;
                        rowDefns.Add(rowDefn2);
                        List<ColumnDefinition> colDefns = new List<ColumnDefinition>();
                        ColumnDefinition colDefn = new ColumnDefinition();
                        colDefn.Width = 100;
                        colDefns.Add(colDefn);
                        ColumnDefinition colDefn2 = new ColumnDefinition();
                        colDefn2.Width = 100;
                        colDefns.Add(colDefn2);
                        grid.SetDefinitions(rowDefns, colDefns);
                        GridCellItem child00 = new GridCellItem();
                        grid.AddObject(child00, 0, 0);
                        GridCellItem child01 = new GridCellItem();
                        grid.AddObject(child01, 0, 1);
                        GridCellItem child10 = new GridCellItem();
                        grid.AddObject(child10, 1, 0);
                        GridCellItem child11 = new GridCellItem();
                        grid.AddObject(child11, 1, 1);
                        basicElements.Add(grid);
                    }
                }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.GridPanel.SetDefinitions(System.Collections.Generic.List{Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.RowDefinition},System.Collections.Generic.List{Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ColumnDefinition})
member.summary: Sets the row and column definitions for the grid panel.
member.param: A list of objects representing the row definitions for the grid.
A list of objects representing the column definitions for the grid.
member.remarks: This method allows you to specify the row and column definitions for the grid panel. The row definitions define the height and behavior of each row in the grid, while the column definitions define the width and behavior of each column. You can define the row and column definitions by providing a list of and objects, respectively. By setting the row and column definitions, you can control how the child elements are positioned and sized within the grid panel.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height = "2000px" Width="850px" BasicElements="@basicElements" >
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code {
                DiagramObjectCollection<CommonElement> basicElements = new DiagramObjectCollection<CommonElement>();
                    protected override void OnInitialized()
                    {
                        GridPanel grid = new GridPanel();
                        grid.OffsetX = 300;
                        grid.OffsetY = 200;
                        List<RowDefinition> rowDefns = new List<RowDefinition>();
                        RowDefinition rowDefn1 = new RowDefinition();
                        rowDefn1.Height = 50;
                        rowDefns.Add(rowDefn1);
                        RowDefinition rowDefn2 = new RowDefinition();
                        rowDefn2.Height = 50;
                        rowDefns.Add(rowDefn2);
                        List<ColumnDefinition> colDefns = new List<ColumnDefinition>();
                        ColumnDefinition colDefn = new ColumnDefinition();
                        colDefn.Width = 100;
                        colDefns.Add(colDefn);
                        ColumnDefinition colDefn2 = new ColumnDefinition();
                        colDefn2.Width = 100;
                        colDefns.Add(colDefn2);
                        grid.SetDefinitions(rowDefns, colDefns);
                        basicElements.Add(grid);
                    }
                }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints
member.summary: Specifies the constraints that enable or disable certain features of the .

remarks.para: The enumeration allows you to control various functionalities of the diagram component including user interactions, zooming, panning, routing, and other behavioral aspects.
This enumeration supports bitwise operations, allowing multiple constraints to be combined.

item.description: - Disables all diagram functionalities
- Enables bridge creation for connectors
- Enables undo/redo functionality
- Enables user interaction with the diagram
- Enables public API updates
- Combines user interaction and API update capabilities
- Enables zooming functionality
- Enables horizontal panning
- Enables vertical panning
- Enables panning in both directions
- Maintains zoom ratio during text editing
- Enables tooltips for diagram elements
- Enables automatic line routing
- Prevents line overlapping
- Enables standard diagram functionalities

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.None
member.summary: Disables all functionalities of the diagram.

remarks.para: When this constraint is applied, the diagram becomes completely non-interactive and all features are disabled.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.Bridging
member.summary: Enables bridge creation for all connectors in the diagram.

remarks.para: When enabled, connectors will automatically create visual bridges when they intersect with other connectors, improving diagram readability.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.UndoRedo
member.summary: Enables or disables the undo or redo functionality for the diagram.

remarks.para: When enabled, users can undo and redo their actions performed on the diagram elements.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.UserInteraction
member.summary: Determines whether user interaction should be enabled for the diagram.

remarks.para: When enabled, users can interact with diagram elements through mouse and keyboard actions such as selection, dragging, and resizing.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.ApiUpdate
member.summary: Determines whether public API updates should be enabled for the diagram.

remarks.para: When enabled, the diagram can be modified through public API methods and property changes.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.PageEditable
member.summary: Enables diagram editing through both and capabilities.

remarks.para: This is a composite constraint that combines and flags.
When applied, the diagram becomes fully editable through both user actions and programmatic API calls.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.Zoom
member.summary: Enables or disables zooming functionality for the diagram.

remarks.para: When enabled, users can zoom in and out of the diagram using mouse wheel, touch gestures, or programmatic zoom methods.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.PanX
member.summary: Enables or disables panning actions only on the x-axis (horizontal panning).

remarks.para: When enabled, users can pan the diagram horizontally using mouse drag or touch gestures.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.PanY
member.summary: Enables or disables panning actions only on the y-axis (vertical panning).

remarks.para: When enabled, users can pan the diagram vertically using mouse drag or touch gestures.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.Pan
member.summary: Enables panning functionality for the diagram in both horizontal and vertical directions.

remarks.para: This is a composite constraint that combines and flags.
When applied, users can pan the diagram in any direction using mouse drag or touch gestures.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.ZoomTextEdit
member.summary: Determines whether the current zoom ratio should be maintained during text editing operations.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramConstraints.Default

This represents the recommended default configuration for most diagram implementations.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.FlipDirection
member.summary: Specifies how the diagram elements have to be flipped.

remarks.para: The enumeration defines the direction in which diagram elements (nodes, connectors, and groups) can be flipped.
This enables the standard set of diagram functionalities for transforming element orientations.

item.description: - Disables all flip behavior and maintains the original orientation
- Mirrors the element across the horizontal axis
- Mirrors the element across the vertical axis
- Mirrors the element across both horizontal and vertical axes

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.FlipDirection.None
member.summary: No flip will be applied to the diagram element.
member.remarks: This is the default value that maintains the original orientation of the diagram element without any mirroring transformation.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.FlipDirection.Horizontal
member.summary: Flips the diagram element horizontally across the horizontal axis.
member.remarks: The element is mirrored horizontally, creating a left-to-right reflection based on the value.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.FlipDirection.Vertical
member.summary: Flips the diagram element vertically across the vertical axis.
member.remarks: The element is mirrored vertically, creating a top-to-bottom reflection based on the value.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.FlipDirection.Both
member.summary: Flips the diagram element both horizontally and vertically.
member.remarks: The element is mirrored across both axes simultaneously, combining horizontal and vertical flip transformations based on the value.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramFlipMode
member.summary: Specifies the flip behavior options for diagram objects.

remarks.para: The enumeration controls which parts of a diagram object are affected when flip operations are performed. This enumeration is applicable only to nodes and node groups.
This is a flags enumeration, allowing multiple flip modes to be combined using bitwise operations.

item.description: - Disables all flip operations
- Flips the node along with annotation, excluding its text
- Flips only the annotation's text, excluding the annotation itself
- Flips the node along with annotation and its text
- Enables flip operations for ports
- Flips the node with port and annotation, excluding text
- Flips the node with port and annotation text, excluding annotation
- Enables flip operations for all components (content, text, and port)

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure flip mode for a diagram node:
Node Node = new Node() { ID = "node1", Width = 100, Height = 100, OffsetX = 100, OffsetY = 300, Flip=FlipDirection.Horizontal, FlipMode=FlipMode.All, };

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramFlipMode.None
member.summary: Disables all the flip operations for the diagram object.

remarks.para: When this value is set, no flip behavior will be applied to any part of the diagram object.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramFlipMode.Content
member.summary: Flips the node along with annotation and its text content.
member.remarks: This is a combination of and modes, providing comprehensive flip behavior for all annotation-related elements.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramFlipMode.Text
member.summary: Flips the node along with annotation’s text only, excluding the annotation itself.
member.remarks: This mode allows the text within annotations to be flipped while maintaining the original orientation of the annotation container.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramFlipMode.Port
member.summary: Enables flip operations for diagram object ports.
member.remarks: When this mode is enabled, the ports attached to the diagram object will be flipped along with the flip operation.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramFlipMode.PortAndLabelOnly
member.summary: Flips the node along with port and the annotation excluding its text.
member.remarks: This mode combines and to flip both ports and annotation containers while preserving text orientation.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramFlipMode.PortWithLabelText
member.summary: Flips the node along with the port and the text of the annotation, excluding the annotation itself.
member.remarks: This mode combines and to flip ports and text content while maintaining annotation container orientation.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramFlipMode.LabelOnly
member.summary: Flips the node along with the annotation, excluding its text.
member.remarks: This mode flips the node along with the annotation.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramFlipMode.All
member.summary: Enables flip operations for diagram object components including content, text, and ports.
member.remarks: This is the most comprehensive flip mode, combining , , and to ensure all parts of the diagram object are affected by flip operations.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.VerticalAlignment
member.summary: Represents the alignment of the diagram elements based on its immediate parent.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes">
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code
            {
                public DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>() { };
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    // A node is created and stored in nodes array.
                    Node Node = new Node()
                    {
                        /// Initialize the port collection
                        Ports = new DiagramObjectCollection<PointPort>()
                        {
                            new PointPort()
                            {
                                VerticalAlignment = VerticalAlignment.Top
                            }
                        },
                    };
                    nodes.Add(Node);
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.BranchDirection
member.summary: Defines the different branch directions available for when using .
member.value: The default values are for and for .
member.remarks:
The available branch directions are:
SameAsFlow: Aligns the branch direction with the flow of the chart.
LeftInFlow: Sets the branch direction to the left relative to the flow.
RightInFlow: Sets the branch direction to the right relative to the flow.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SubTreeAlignmentType
member.summary: Specifies the collection of sub tree alignments in an organizational chart.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height = "600px" NodeCreating="@NodeDefaults" ConnectorCreating="@ConnectorDefaults">
                <DataSourceSettings ID = "Id" ParentID="Team" DataSource="@DataSource"></DataSourceSettings>   
                <Layout Type = "LayoutType.OrganizationalChart"
                        @bind-HorizontalSpacing="@HorizontalSpacing" 
                        @bind-VerticalSpacing="@VerticalSpacing" 
                        GetLayoutInfo="GetLayoutInfo">
                </Layout>
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code
            {
               public class OrgChartDataModel 
               {
                   public string Id  { get; set; }
                   public string Team { get; set; }
                   public string Role { get; set; }
               }
               public object DataSource = new List<object>()
               {
                   new OrgChartDataModel() { Id= "1", Role= "General Manager" },
                   new OrgChartDataModel() { Id= "2", Role= "Human Resource Manager", Team= "1" },
                   new OrgChartDataModel() { Id= "3", Role= "Design Manager", Team= "1" },
                   new OrgChartDataModel() { Id= "4", Role= "Operation Manager", Team= "1" },
                   new OrgChartDataModel() { Id= "5", Role= "Marketing Manager", Team= "1" }
               };
            }

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SubTreeAlignmentType.Right
member.summary: Aligns the child nodes at the right of the parent in a horizontal/vertical sub tree.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SubTreeAlignmentType.Center
member.summary: Aligns the child nodes at the center of the parent in a horizontal sub tree.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SubTreeAlignmentType.Alternate
member.summary: Aligns the child nodes alternatively on both left and right sides in a vertical sub tree.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SubTreeAlignmentType.Balanced
member.summary: Aligns the child nodes horizontally to balance the width and height of the sub tree.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramOverviewConstraints
member.summary: Specifies the interaction setting (such as the zoom, pan, draw, and tap) enabled or disabled in overview component.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent @ref = "diagram" Height="600px" Width="90%" ID="diagram" @bind-Nodes="nodes"
                                @bind-Connectors="connectors">
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            <SfDiagramOverviewComponent Width = "400" Height="300" SourceID="diagram" Constraints="DiagramOverviewConstraints.Zoom"></SfDiagramOverviewComponent>
            @code {
                SfDiagramComponent diagram; DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes; DiagramObjectCollection<Connector> connectors;
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
                    connectors = new DiagramObjectCollection<Connector>();
                    Node node1 = new Node()
                    {
                        ID = "node1",
                        Height = 100,
                        Width = 100,
                        OffsetX = 100,
                        OffsetY = 100,
                        Style = new ShapeStyle()
                        {
                            Fill = "#6BA5D7",
                            StrokeColor = "white",
                            StrokeWidth = 1
                        }
                    };
                    Node node2 = new Node()
                    {
                        ID = "node2",
                        Height = 100,
                        Width = 100,
                        OffsetX = 300,
                        OffsetY = 100,
                        Style = new ShapeStyle()
                        {
                            Fill = "#6BA5D7",
                            StrokeColor = "white",
                            StrokeWidth = 1
                        }
                    };
                    nodes.Add(node1); nodes.Add(node2);
                    Connector connector1 = new Connector()
                    {
                        ID = "connector1",
                        SourceID = "node1",
                        TargetID = "node2",
                        Type = ConnectorSegmentType.Straight,
                        Style = new ShapeStyle()
                        {
                            Fill = "#6BA5D7",
                            StrokeWidth = 2
                        }
                    };
                    connectors.Add(connector1);
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SizeChangingEventArgs
member.summary: Notifies when the element is resizing.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes" SizeChanging="@OnSizeChange" />
            @code
            {
                DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes;
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
                    Node node = new Node()
                    {
                        // Position of the node
                        OffsetX = 250,
                        OffsetY = 250,
                        // Size of the node
                        Width = 100,
                        Height = 100,
                    };
                    nodes.Add(node);
                }
                // Size change event for the diagram
                public void OnSizeChange(SizeChangingEventArgs args)
                {
                    Console.WriteLine(args.NewValue.Nodes[0].ID);
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SizeChangedEventArgs
member.summary: Notifies when the element is resized.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes" SizeChanged="@SizeChanged" />
            @code
            {
                // To define the node collection
                DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes;
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
                    // A node is created and stored in the nodes collection.
                    Node node = new Node()
                    {
                        // Position of the node
                        OffsetX = 250,
                        OffsetY = 250,
                        // Size of the node
                        Width = 100,
                        Height = 100,
                        Style = new ShapeStyle() { Fill = "#6BA5D7", StrokeColor = "white" }
                    };
                    // Add a node
                    nodes.Add(node);
                }
                // Size change event for the diagram
                public void SizeChanged(SizeChangedEventArgs args)
                {
                    Console.WriteLine(args.NewValue.Nodes[0].ID);
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager
member.summary: Represents the manager that handles undo and redo operations for a diagram, notifying when changes are reverted or restored.
member.remarks: The is crucial for maintaining the state of a diagram by allowing users to undo and redo changes.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.Diagram
member.summary: Gets or sets instance of SfDiagramComponent.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.ChildContent
member.summary: Gets or sets the child content for the history manager.
member.remarks: Allows customization of the history manager's content using render fragments, enabling dynamic and flexible UI updates within the diagram component. It supports customization of the user interface by defining children elements that are rendered dynamically.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.CanUndo
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the history entry can be undone.
member.remarks: Setting this property to allows the history manager to revert the most recent action, ensuring that accidental changes can be easily undone to restore previous states.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.CanRedo
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the history entry can be redone.
member.remarks: When set to , the history manager enables reapplying the last undone action, facilitating the reinstatement of changes that were reversed, thus enhancing the flexibility of the undo-redo workflow.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.CurrentEntry
member.summary: Gets or sets the current entry object.
member.remarks: Represents the specific history entry currently active within the diagram's history stack, allowing users to query or modify the current state of the undo and redo operations.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.Push(Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.HistoryEntryBase)
member.summary: Stores a history entry on the history list.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.Undo
member.summary: Gets or sets the callback method that is invoked when a custom entry is in the undo stage.
member.remarks: Allows integration of custom logic during the undo operation within the diagram component, enhancing the flexibility and control over undo actions.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Width="800px" Height="800px">
                <DiagramHistoryManager Undo="onCustomUndo"></DiagramHistoryManager>
            </SfDiagramComponent >
            @code
            {
                private void onCustomUndo(HistoryEntryBase entry)
                {
                    (entry.RedoObject) = entry.UndoObject.Clone() as Node;
                    (entry.UndoObject as Node).AdditionalInfo[(entry.UndoObject as Node).ID] = "Start";
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.Redo
member.summary: Gets or sets the callback method that is invoked when a custom entry is in the redo stage.
member.remarks: Allows integration of custom logic during the redo operation within the diagram component, enhancing the flexibility and control over redo actions.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Width="800px" Height="800px">
                <DiagramHistoryManager Redo="onCustomRedo"></DiagramHistoryManager>
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code
            {
                private void onCustomRedo(HistoryEntryBase entry)
                {
                    Node current = entry.UndoObject.Clone() as Node;
                    (entry.UndoObject as Node).AdditionalInfo[(entry.UndoObject as Node).ID] = "Description";
                    entry.RedoObject = current;
                }
            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.StartGroupAction
member.summary: Initiates a group action allowing you to revert or restore multiple changes through a single undo/redo command within the .

remarks.para: This method starts the grouping of changes, which is useful for managing multiple related modifications in a unified manner using undo/redo functionality.

example.code: // Start the grouping of changes diagram.StartGroupAction();

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.EndGroupAction
member.summary: Ends a group action which encapsulates multiple changes for combined undo/redo operations within the .

remarks.para: This method finalizes the grouping of changes, allowing them to be treated as a single action in the undo/redo sequence, thus enhancing the user's control over multiple related modifications.

example.code: // End the grouping of changes diagram.EndGroupAction();

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramHistoryManager.HistoryAdding
member.summary: Gets or sets a callback that occurs determining if changes should be stored in the history.
member.remarks: This event is triggered before a change is added to the history, allowing you to decide whether it should be committed.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Width="800px" Height="800px">
                <DiagramHistoryManager HistoryAdding="OnHistoryAdding"></DiagramHistoryManager>
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code
            {
                private void OnHistoryAdding(HistoryAddingEventArgs args)
                {
                    args.Cancel = true;
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.NodeBase.SearchTags
member.summary: Gets or sets the keywords used to search for symbols in the symbol palette. These keywords are associated with nodes, connectors, groups, swimlanes, and BPMN symbols.
member.value: A of containing the search keywords for symbol palette filtering. The default value is an empty collection.

remarks.para: The property enables efficient symbol discovery in the symbol palette by providing searchable keywords.

When users type in the symbol palette search box, symbols with matching tags in their collection will be displayed. This improves user experience by allowing quick access to relevant symbols without browsing through all available options.
Multiple keywords can be assigned to a single symbol to increase its discoverability across different search contexts.

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set search tags for a to make it discoverable in the symbol palette:
Node node = new Node() { OffsetX = 250, OffsetY = 250, Width = 100, Height = 100, ID = "Node", SearchTags = new List<string>() { "Node", "Basic" }, Style = new ShapeStyle() { Fill = "#6495ED", StrokeColor = "white" }, };

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.NodeBase.IgnoreSearchTags
member.summary: Gets or sets the keywords associated with nodes, connectors, groups, and swimlane symbols defined in ignore tags. These keywords are used to exclude symbols while searching in the symbol palette.
member.value: The default value of IgnoreSearchTags is an empty list. This property specifies the list of ignored search tags used to exclude certain symbols from search results in the symbol palette.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ConnectorSegment
member.summary: Represents the segment of the connector. This class is a fundamental part of the connector structure used to visualize connections between diagram nodes.

remarks.para: This class is essential for handling the structural segments of a connector, typically used in diagram components to connect different nodes or points in a diagram. It supports various segment types, such as straight lines or complex paths.
Each segment can be customized by setting properties such as the segment type, whether it allows dragging, and the specific points it connects.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Connectors="@connectors">
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code
            {
                public DiagramObjectCollection<Connector> connectors = new DiagramObjectCollection<Connector>();
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    Connector connector = new Connector()
                    {
                        ID = "straight",
                        SourcePoint = new DiagramPoint() { X = 100, Y = 200 },
                        TargetPoint = new DiagramPoint() { X = 300, Y = 200 },
                        Segments = new DiagramObjectCollection<ConnectorSegment>()
                        {
                            // Create a new straight segment 
                            new StraightSegment() { Point = new DiagramPoint(420, 300) },
                        }
                    };
                    connectors.Add(connector);
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DataSourceSettings
member.summary: Represents the settings that specify the data source and define how the parent and child relationship will be generated in the diagram layout. It is applicable only when a diagram layout is used.

remarks.para: This class is a part of the diagram component and allows the configuration of the data source used in the layout.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Width="1000px" Height="1000px">
                <DataSourceSettings @bind-DataSource="@data" ID="@Id" ParentID="@ParentId" SymbolMapping="@doBinding"></DataSourceSettings>
                <Layout Type="LayoutType">
                </Layout>
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code {
                public object data { get; set; }
                public string Id;
                public string ParentId;
                public LayoutType LayoutType = LayoutType.HierarchicalTree;
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    Id = "Name";
                    ParentId = "Category";
                    data = Data1;
                }
                // Bind the external data with the node
                private Node doBinding(Node node, object data)
                {
                    HierarchicalDetails hierarchicalData = data as HierarchicalDetails;
                    node.Annotations = new DiagramObjectCollection<ShapeAnnotation>()
                    {
                        new ShapeAnnotation()
                        {
                            ID = "annotation" + node.ID,
                            Content = hierarchicalData.Name,
                        },
                    };
                    return node;
                }
                public List<HierarchicalDetails> Data1 = new List<HierarchicalDetails>()
                {
                    new HierarchicalDetails(){ Name = "Diagram", FillColor = "#916DAF" },
                    new HierarchicalDetails(){ Name = "Layout", Category = "Diagram" },
                    new HierarchicalDetails(){ Name = "Tree Layout", Category = "Layout" },
                    new HierarchicalDetails(){ Name = "Organizational Chart", Category = "Layout" }
                };
                public class HierarchicalDetails
                {
                    public string Name { get; set; }
                    public string Category { get; set; }
                    public string FillColor { get; set; }
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.CommandManager
member.summary: Represents the manager that handles a collection of custom commands and their associated key gestures in a diagram component.

remarks.para: The class facilitates the definition and execution of custom commands in response to particular key gestures. This is especially useful for implementing keyboard shortcuts to enhance user interaction with diagram components.
Custom commands must be registered with their specific and should adhere to a consistent naming convention to avoid command collisions.

example.para: The following code example demonstrates how to set up a diagram with custom commands for grouping and ungrouping nodes using specific keyboard shortcuts.
example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent @ref="@diagram" Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes">
                 @* Initializing the custom commands *@
                 <CommandManager Commands="@command" Execute="@CommandExecute" CanExecute="@CanExe">
                 </CommandManager>
             </SfDiagramComponent>
             @code {
                 // Reference to the diagram component
                 SfDiagramComponent diagram;
                 // Defining custom keyboard commands
                 DiagramObjectCollection<KeyboardCommand> command = new DiagramObjectCollection<KeyboardCommand>()
                 {
                     new Command()
                     {
                         Name = "CustomGroup",
                         Gesture = new KeyGesture() { Key = DiagramKeys.G, KeyModifiers = KeyModifiers.Control }
                     },
                     new Command()
                     {
                         Name = "CustomUngroup",
                         Gesture = new KeyGesture() { Key = DiagramKeys.U, KeyModifiers = KeyModifiers.Control }
                     },
                 };
                 // Define the nodes collection for the diagram
                 DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
            
                 // Determines if the command can be executed
                 public void CanExe(CommandKeyArgs args)
                 {
                     args.CanExecute = true;
                 }
                 // Executes the custom command based on the gesture
                 public void CommandExecute(CommandKeyArgs args)
                 {
                     if (args.Gesture.KeyModifiers == KeyModifiers.Control && args.Gesture.Key == DiagramKeys.G)
                     {
                         // Custom command to group the selected nodes
                         diagram.Group();
                     }
                     else if (args.Gesture.KeyModifiers == KeyModifiers.Control && args.Gesture.Key == DiagramKeys.U)
                     {
                         Selector selector = diagram.SelectedItems;
                         // Custom command to ungroup the selected items
                         if (selector.Nodes.Count > 0 && selector.Nodes[0] is Group)
                         {
                             if ((selector.Nodes[0] as Group).Children.Length > 0)
                             {
                                 diagram.Ungroup();
                             }
                         }
                     }
                 }
             }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.KeyboardCommand
member.summary: Represents a command associated with a keyboard gesture within a diagram component.

remarks.para: This class is utilized primarily to define keyboard shortcuts within a diagram. Each command is tied to a specific key gesture, which is used for triggering operations such as grouping or ungrouping diagram elements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.KeyboardCommand.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of the command.
member.value: A representing the name of the command. The default value is an empty string.
member.remarks: This property is essential for identifying the command within the diagram's command manager. Command names should be unique to avoid conflicts when assigning multiple commands.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent @ref="@diagram" Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes">
            @* Initializing the custom commands*@
                <CommandManager Commands = "@command">
                </CommandManager>
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code
            {
                // Reference to the diagram
                SfDiagramComponent diagram;
                DiagramObjectCollection<KeyboardCommand> command = new DiagramObjectCollection<KeyboardCommand>()
                {
                    new Command()
                    {
                        Name = "CustomGroup",
                        Gesture = new KeyGesture() { Key = DiagramKeys.G,  Modifiers = ModifierKeys.Control }
                    },
                    new Command()
                    {
                        Name = "CustomUngroup",
                        Gesture = new KeyGesture() { Key = DiagramKeys.U,  Modifiers = ModifierKeys.Control }
                    },
                };
              }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramIcon
member.summary: Represents the icon of a node in the diagram.

remarks.para: The is used to display icons that allow nodes to be expanded or collapsed. This is particularly useful in scenarios where nodes have child nodes that can be shown or hidden.
Use the ExpandIcon and CollapseIcon properties to customize the appearance and behavior of these icons.

example.para: This example demonstrates how to initialize a node with Expand and Collapse icons in a diagram component.
example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes" />
             @code {
                 // Initialize the node collection with nodes and expand/collapse icons
                 DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
            
                 protected override void OnInitialized()
                 {
                     Node node1 = new Node()
                     {
                         ID = "node1",
                         // Size of the node
                         Height = 100,
                         Width = 100,
                         // Position of the node
                         OffsetX = 100,
                         OffsetY = 100,
                         ExpandIcon = new DiagramExpandIcon()
                         {
                             Shape = DiagramExpandIcons.Minus,
                             Fill = "Grey",
                             Margin = new DiagramThickness
                             {
                                 Top = 1,
                                 Bottom = 1,
                                 Left = 1,
                                 Right = 1,
                             },
                             Width = 10,
                             Height = 10,
                             OffsetX = 0.5,
                             OffsetY = 1,
                             HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Center,
                             VerticalAlignment = VerticalAlignment.Center,
                             BorderColor = "Red",
                             BorderWidth = 3,
                             CornerRadius = 3,
                             Padding = new DiagramThickness
                             {
                                 Top = 1,
                                 Bottom = 1,
                                 Left = 1,
                                 Right = 1,
                             }
                         },
                         CollapseIcon = new DiagramCollapseIcon()
                         {
                             Shape = DiagramCollapseIcons.Plus,
                             Fill = "Grey",
                             Margin = new DiagramThickness
                             {
                                 Top = 1,
                                 Bottom = 1,
                                 Left = 1,
                                 Right = 1,
                             },
                             Width = 10,
                             Height = 10,
                             OffsetX = 0.5,
                             OffsetY = 1,
                             HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Center,
                             VerticalAlignment = VerticalAlignment.Center,
                             BorderColor = "Red",
                             BorderWidth = 3,
                             CornerRadius = 3,
                             Padding = new DiagramThickness
                             {
                                 Top = 1,
                                 Bottom = 1,
                                 Left = 1,
                                 Right = 1,
                             }
                         }
                     };
                     nodes.Add(node1);
                 }
             }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramIcon.OffsetX
member.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal offset for the Expand/Collapse Icon in a diagram node.
member.value: A representing the horizontal position of the icon. The value should be between 0 and 1, where 0 aligns the icon to the left edge and 1 aligns it to the right edge. The default value is 0.5.

remarks.para: Defines the position of the Expand/Collapse icon with respect to the boundaries of a node within a diagram. Adjusting the offset can help in better alignment of the icon based on the design needs of the diagram.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes" />
            @code
            {
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    Node node1 = new Node()
                    {
                        ExpandIcon = new DiagramExpandIcon()
                        {
                            Shape = DiagramExpandIcons.Minus,
                            Fill = "Grey",
                            Width = 10,
                            Height = 10,
                            OffsetX = 0.5,
                            OffsetY = 1,
                        },
                    };
                    nodes.Add(node1);
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramIcon.OffsetY
member.summary: Gets or sets the Y coordinate offset of the Expand/Collapse icon.
member.value: A representing the offset coordinate along the Y-axis. The default value is 0.0.

remarks.para: This property defines the Y position of the Expand/Collapse icon relative to the boundaries of a node. Adjusting this offset allows you to reposition the icon vertically to fit within custom layouts or designs.

example.b: Example of setting the OffsetY property:
example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes" />
            @code {
                DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
                protected override void OnInitialized() {
                    Node node1 = new Node() {
                        ExpandIcon = new DiagramExpandIcon() {
                            Shape = DiagramExpandIcons.Minus,
                            Fill = "Grey",
                            Width = 10,
                            Height = 10,
                            OffsetX = 0.5,
                            OffsetY = 1,
                        },
                    };
                    nodes.Add(node1);
                }
            }

member.summary: Gets or sets the fill color of an icon. Represents the color used to fill the icon's background.
member.value: A representing the color value of the icon fill. The default value is .

remarks.para: Setting this property changes the visual appearance of the icon within the diagram node, allowing customization to match application themes or specific design requirements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramIcon.Margin
member.summary: Gets or sets the margin for the Expand/Collapse Icon.
member.value: A representing the space around the icon. The default values are 0 on all sides.

remarks.para: Defines the offset space from the actual position of the icon, allowing custom placement within its container.
Adjust the margin to control the spacing from other elements.

                DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
                protected override void OnInitialized() {
                    Node node1 = new Node() {
                        ExpandIcon = new DiagramExpandIcon() {
                            Shape = DiagramExpandIcons.Minus,
                            Fill = "Grey",
                            Margin = new DiagramThickness() {
                                Top = 1,
                                Bottom = 1,
                                Left = 1,
                                Right = 1,
                            }
                        },
                    };
                    nodes.Add(node1);
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramIcon.HorizontalAlignment
member.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal alignment of the Expand/Collapse Icon.
member.value: A value that determines the horizontal position of the icon. The possible values are Left, Center, Right, and Stretch. The default value is HorizontalAlignment.Center.

remarks.para: This value specifies how the Expand/Collapse Icon is aligned horizontally. It defines the position of the icon along the horizontal axis within its designated space.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes" />
            @code {
                // Initialize the node collection with a node and configure the Expand & Collapse icon
                DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
                protected override void OnInitialized() {
                    Node node1 = new Node() {
                        ExpandIcon = new DiagramExpandIcon() {
                            HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Center,
                        },
                    };
                    nodes.Add(node1);
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramIcon.VerticalAlignment
member.summary: Gets or sets the vertical alignment of the expand/collapse icon in the diagram node.
member.value: A value that specifies the vertical positioning of the expand/collapse icon. The default value is .

remarks.para: Determines how the icon is aligned vertically within the node bounds. Accepted values are from the enumeration, including , , and .

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramIcon.PathData
member.summary: Gets or sets the custom geometry data that defines the visual path of the expand or collapse icon in a node.
member.value: A representing the SVG path data for a custom-shaped expand or collapse icon. The default value is .

remarks.para: Set the property to specify a custom shape for the expand/collapse icon when is assigned to the icon’s shape property. The path data uses SVG notation and determines how the custom icon will be rendered.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramIcon.CornerRadius
member.summary: Gets or sets the corner radius of the expand/collapse icon.
member.value: A representing the corner radius of the expand/collapse icon. The default value is 0.

remarks.para: Use this property to round the corners of the expand or collapse icon. Setting a higher value produces more pronounced rounded corners, while a value of 0 maintains sharp (square) corners.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramIcon.Padding
member.summary: Gets or sets the padding of the expand/collapse icon.
member.value: A that specifies the space by which the icon is offset from its border. The default value is a with all sides set to 0.

remarks.para: Padding adds space between the icon content and its border area. Use this property to adjust the alignment of the icon within its node to prevent overlap with other elements.

member.summary: Represents the expand icon used to indicate the expandable state of a node in a diagram component.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramExpandIcon.Shape
member.summary: Gets or sets the shape of the Expand Icon.
member.value: A representing the shape of the Expand Icon. The default value is .

remarks.para: The Diagram provides built-in , including Minus, ArrowUp, and Template, among others.
Custom shapes, such as Path Shape, can also be applied to the Expand Icon.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes" />
            @code
            {
                //Initialize the node collection with nodes and Expand & CollapseIcons
                DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    Node node = new Node()
                    {
                        ExpandIcon = new DiagramExpandIcon()
                        {
                            Shape = DiagramExpandIcons.Minus,
                        },
                        CollapseIcon = new DiagramCollapseIcon()
                        {
                            Shape = DiagramExpandIcons.Path,
                            PathData = "M100,200 C100,100 250,100 250,200 S400,300 400,200",
                        }
                    };
                    nodes.Add(node);
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.NodeGroup
member.summary: Represents a cluster of multiple nodes and connectors into a single element, functioning as a container for its children (nodes, groups, and connectors).
member.remarks: This class allows for the logical grouping of multiple diagram objects, making it easier to manage and manipulate related nodes and connectors as a single unit.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="500px" @ref="diagram" Nodes="@nodes">
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code
            {
                SfDiagramComponent diagram;
                DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    Node node1 = createNode("node1", 100, 100);
                    Node node2 = createNode("node2", 300, 100);
                    NodeGroup groupNode = new NodeGroup();
                    // Grouping node 1 and node 2 into a single group
                    groupNode.Children = new string[] { "node1", "node2" };
                    nodes.Add(node1);
                    nodes.Add(node2);
                    nodes.Add(groupNode);
                }
                public Node createNode(string id, double offsetX, double offsetY)
                {
                    Node node = new Node()
                    {
                        ID = id,
                        OffsetX = offsetX,
                        OffsetY = offsetY,
                        Height = 100,
                        Width = 100,
                        Style = new ShapeStyle() { Fill = "#6495ED" }
                    };
                    return node;
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramSelectionSettings
member.summary: Represents a visual representation of the selected elements. Provides functionality as a container for single or multiple selected elements in a diagram structure.
member.remarks: This class facilitates the manipulation and organization of selected elements within a diagram.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramSelectionSettings.Nodes
member.summary: Gets or sets a collection of selected nodes within the diagram.
member.value: An instance representing the selected nodes. The default value is an empty collection.

remarks.para: This property is used to access or manipulate the nodes selected in the diagram component.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent ref="@diagram" Height="600px" Nodes="@nodes" />
             @code
             {
                 SfDiagramComponent diagram;
                 DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
                 protected override void OnInitialized()
                 {
                     Node node = new Node()
                     {
                         ID = "node1",
                         // Size of the node
                         Height = 100,
                         Width = 100,
                         // Position of the node
                         OffsetX = 100,
                         OffsetY = 100,
                     };
                     nodes.Add(node);
                     diagram.SelectionSettings.Nodes[0].Constraints |= NodeConstraints.AspectRatio;
                 }
             }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.DiagramSelectionSettings.Connectors
member.summary: Gets or sets the collection of selected connectors in the diagram.
member.value: An representing the selected connectors. The default value is an empty collection.
member.remarks: This property contains the connectors that are currently selected within the diagram component.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent ref="@diagram" Height="600px" Connectors="@nodes" />
            @code {
                SfDiagramComponent diagram;
                DiagramObjectCollection<Connector> connectors = new DiagramObjectCollection<Connector>();
                protected override void OnInitialized() {
                    Connector connector = new Connector() {
                        ID = "connector1",
                        Type = ConnectorSegmentType.Straight,
                        SourcePoint = new DiagramPoint() { X = 100, Y = 100 },
                        TargetPoint = new DiagramPoint() { X = 200, Y = 200 },
                    };
                    connectors.Add(connector);
                    diagram.SelectionSettings.Connectors[0].Constraints |= ConnectorConstraints.Delete;
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SfDiagramComponent
member.summary: Represents a comprehensive diagramming component that provides functionality for creating, editing, and rendering interactive diagrams with nodes, connectors, and various diagramming features.

remarks.para: The serves as the main container for all diagramming operations, including node management, connector routing, layout algorithms, and user interactions.
It handles rendering, event management, serialization, and provides extensive customization options for appearance and behavior.
Key features include drag-and-drop operations, automatic layout algorithms, undo/redo functionality, clipboard operations, and export capabilities to various formats.

member.summary: Renders the diagram. It contains all the properties of the diagram to be rendered.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SfDiagramComponent.HistoryManager
member.summary: Gets or sets the history manager for the that handles undo and redo operations.
member.value: A that manages the history of changes made to the diagram. The default value is a new instance of .

remarks.para: The history manager tracks all changes made to the diagram and provides functionality to undo and redo operations.
It maintains a stack of history entries that can be navigated through programmatically or via user interactions.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SfDiagramComponent.Tooltip
member.summary: Gets or sets the tooltip that should be shown when the mouse hovers over nodes or connectors in the .
member.value: A representing the tooltip configuration for the diagram. The default value is .

remarks.para: The diagram tooltip is displayed when nodes and connectors have their constraint values set to "InheritTooltip".
Individual nodes and connectors can override this diagram-level tooltip by setting their own properties.
The tooltip appears on mouse hover and provides contextual information about diagram elements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SfDiagramComponent.BridgeDirection
member.summary: Gets or sets the direction of the bridge that is inserted when connector segments intersect in the .
member.value: A enumeration value specifying the direction of the bridge when connector segments intersect. The default value is .

remarks.para: Bridge direction determines the visual appearance of connector intersections by controlling which direction the bridge arc faces.

item.description: - Creates bridges that arc toward the left side of the intersection
- Creates bridges that arc toward the right side of the intersection
- Creates bridges that arc toward the top of the intersection
- Creates bridges that arc toward the bottom of the intersection

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set the bridge direction for connector intersections.
<SfDiagramComponent Height="900px" Width="1200px" BridgeDirection="Direction.Right" Connectors="@connectors"> </SfDiagramComponent>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SfDiagramComponent.ID
member.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier of the .
member.value: A representing the unique identifier for the diagram component. The default value is a randomly generated string.

remarks.para: The ID property serves as a unique identifier for the diagram component instance, enabling programmatic access and reference to the specific diagram.
This identifier is automatically generated if not explicitly provided.

member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set a custom ID for the diagram component.
<SfDiagramComponent Height="900px" Width="1200px" ID="myCustomDiagram"> </SfDiagramComponent>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SfDiagramComponent.BridgeDirectionChanged
member.summary: Gets or sets the callback that is invoked when the bridge direction of the changes.
member.value: An that is triggered when the bridge direction is modified. The default value is an empty event callback.

remarks.para: Use this callback to respond to changes in the connector bridge direction and apply related UI updates or business logic.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SfDiagramComponent.DataSourceSettings
member.summary: Gets or sets the data source configuration for binding external data to the .
member.value: A object that configures the data binding properties for the diagram. The default value is .

remarks.para: The enables automatic generation of diagram nodes and connectors from data sources. This is particularly useful for creating automatic layouts.
When configured, the diagram will automatically create nodes based on the data source items and establish parent-child relationships using the specified ID and ParentID properties.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.SfDiagramComponent.Model
member.summary: Gets or sets the diagram model used to generate and render the diagram.
member.value: A instance that defines the structure and content of the diagram. Currently supports for UML sequence diagram generation. The default value is null.
member.remarks: Currently, only UML sequence diagram generation is supported using this model.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent Height="600px" Model="@umlModel">
            </SfDiagramComponent>
            @code
            {
                DiagramModel umlModel;
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                umlModel = new UmlSequenceDiagramModel()
                {
                    Participants = new List<UmlSequenceParticipant>()
                    {
                        new UmlSequenceParticipant()
                        {
                            ID = "User",
                            Content= "User",
                            ShowDestructionMarker= true,
                            IsActor= true,
                            ActivationBoxes= new List<UmlSequenceActivationBox>()
                            {
                                new UmlSequenceActivationBox() { ID = "act1", StartMessageID= "MSG1", EndMessageID= "MSG3" }
                            }
                        },
                        new UmlSequenceParticipant()
                        {
                            ID = "Server",
                            Content= "Server",
                            ShowDestructionMarker= true,
                            IsActor= false,
                            ActivationBoxes= new List<UmlSequenceActivationBox>()
                            {
                                new UmlSequenceActivationBox() { ID = "act2", StartMessageID= "MSG1", EndMessageID= "MSG3" }
                            }
                        }
                    },
                    Messages = new List<UmlSequenceMessage>()
                    {
                        new UmlSequenceMessage()
                        {
                            ID = "MSG1",
                            Content = "User sends request",
                            FromParticipantID = "User",
                            ToParticipantID = "Server"
                        },
                        new UmlSequenceMessage()
                        {
                            ID = "MSG2",
                            Content = "Processing",
                            FromParticipantID = "Server",
                            ToParticipantID = "Server"
                        },
                        new UmlSequenceMessage()
                        {
                            ID = "MSG3",
                            Content = "Server sends response",
                            FromParticipantID = "Server",
                            ToParticipantID = "User"
                        }
                    },
                    Fragments = new List<UmlSequenceFragment>()
                    {
                        new UmlSequenceFragment()
                        {
                            ID = "frag1",
                            Type = UmlSequenceFragmentType.Optional,
                            Conditions = new List<UmlSequenceFragmentCondition>()
                            {
                                new UmlSequenceFragmentCondition()
                                {
                                    Content = "Interactions",
                                    MessageIds = new List<string>(){"MSG1", "MSG2", "MSG3"}
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    };
                }
            }

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable support for chunk messages in the .
